the time taken by humans to categorize an image of an object can be predicted from the perceived similarities of the object with other objects within and outside the same category, and this is consistent with the idea that humans use coarse object representations to categorize images.

the similarity of an item to its category members and to other items in the visual environment determines how quickly we categorize it, and this similarity is based on a shared representation of coarse object structure.

categorization is not a simple process of comparing an object to other members of its category, but instead is based on the perceived similarities of an object to members both within and outside the target category.
